query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing Pd or Pt with Ir in an equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy will induce a controlled tetragonal lattice distortion via stronger spin–orbit coupling, thus enhancing magnetocrystalline anisotropy and increasing coercivity relative to the soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys (e.g., FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt) that crystallize in the fcc structure with low coercivity and high saturation magnetization.
generation.intervention: Substitute Pd or Pt with Ir to create an equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy.
generation.conditions: The alloy should be synthesized under controlled conditions (e.g., rapid solidification followed by annealing at near-room temperature) that stabilize the fcc phase while allowing a slight tetragonal distortion without triggering phase separation or major entropy loss.
generation.structural_mediator: A modest tetragonal distortion of the fcc lattice induced by Ir substitution.
generation.mechanism: Ir has a stronger spin–orbit coupling than Pd or Pt. Its substitution in the FeCoNi matrix is expected to locally break the high symmetry of the fcc structure, creating anisotropic lattice strains. These changes enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy, which in turn raises the energy barrier for domain wall motion and leads to increased coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiIr alloy will display a higher coercive field than the baseline FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt systems while maintaining comparable high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys (such as FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt) that exhibit soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected to hold when the substitution is made in a compositionally nearly equiatomic, high-entropy alloy that retains a predominantly fcc phase. Any significant deviation from equiatomic composition or formation of secondary phases (that reduce configurational entropy) could negate the effect.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of coercivity enhancement remains uncertain because it depends on the precise processing conditions and the degree of induced lattice distortion.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy using rapid solidification and a controlled annealing process, ensuring retention of the high-entropy fcc phase. Prepare control samples of FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt using similar conditions. Characterize the microstructure using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to detect any lattice distortions. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature to determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: X-ray diffraction for phase and lattice parameter analysis
Transmission electron microscopy for detecting lattice distortions
Magnetic hysteresis loops to obtain coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the measured coercivity of the FeCoNiIr alloy is not significantly higher than that of the FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt baselines, or if no measurable tetragonal distortion or associated anisotropy enhancement is observed in the microstructural analyses.

cited_evidence.text: While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

frame.system: A face‐centred cubic (fcc) FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy system, originally in an equiatomic multicomponent state (e.g., FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, FeCoNiPt) that exhibits soft ferromagnetism.
frame.goal: Achieve a higher coercive field (i.e. enhanced magnetic hardness) relative to the baseline soft ferromagnetic FeCoNi and its Pd/Pt derivatives while maintaining high saturation magnetization and qualifying high configurational entropy.
frame.limitation: Prior derivatives (FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt) met the equiatomic and entropy criteria but still yielded soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
root_cause_cues: qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
constraints: Composition must remain nearly equiatomic across all alloying elements
The alloy must retain a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
The modification should be a single intervention within the FeCoNi-based system
frame.regime: The intervention is to be applied under conditions that stabilize the fcc phase at or near room temperature, with controlled processing (e.g., rapid solidification and subsequent annealing) to manage potential lattice distortions.
prior_attempts: FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys were studied, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism (i.e., low coercivity) despite meeting the configurational and compositional criteria.
frame.understanding: The hypothesis is that a judicious compositional substitution in the high-entropy matrix can induce subtle lattice distortions (e.g., a controlled tetragonal distortion) and enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy, thereby increasing coercivity. Whereas Pd and Pt maintain a relatively symmetric fcc environment leading to soft behavior, substituting with an element that has stronger spin–orbit coupling and a propensity to create anisotropic lattice strains (for example, a small addition of Ir) can promote the formation of a slightly less symmetric local environment. This can increase energy barriers against domain wall motion, thus raising the coercivity relative to the FeCoNi baseline.
frame.method: Prepare an equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy (replacing Pd or Pt with Ir) under controlled solidification and annealing conditions to stabilize the desired high-entropy fcc phase with a slight tetragonal distortion. Measure and compare its hysteresis loop and coercive field against those of FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt. A discriminating experiment involves characterizing the microstructure (using XRD and TEM to detect any induced lattice distortion) and magnetic hysteresis at room temperature. The hypothesis will be falsified if the FeCoNiIr alloy exhibits coercivity no greater than that of the reported Pd/Pt alloys or if no measurable lattice distortion is detected.
